messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] P1 - surge of OOM/container restarts in svc-infer-prod (us-west-2). 12 nodes reporting container exit in last 5m. Error class: CUDA OOM + allocator paged-attn fragmentation. Pager -> @oncall-alex. Link: https://alerts.redwood.local/alert/3580011111

oncall-alex: taking it. seeing spikes in OOMs and node restarts. rolling logs now. any early customer impact visibility?

eng-sre-jess: grabbing node-level metrics. early look: memory pressure on GPU host visible, dmesg shows repeated cuda: out of memory and kernel messages about "OOM killer invoked" on containerd processes. sending full kernel tail.

eng-runtime-sam: past incidents like this were paged-attn allocator slow-creep -> fragmentation -> eventually OOM. symptoms line up: gradual memory climb + per-container fragmentation in KV cache. Also saw similar on 1799991234.

infra-robin: listing pods:```
$ kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide | grep svc-infer
svc-infer-abcde-1   0/1   CrashLoopBackOff   3   5m
svc-infer-abcde-2   0/1   CrashLoopBackOff   4   6m
svc-infer-xyz12-4   1/1   Running           0   25m
```
Pods crash with container exit code 137 in many cases.

eng-runtime-sam: tailing container logs from a crashed instance:```
[2026-02-12T01:12:10Z] runtime: attention_paged_allocator: allocate_page failed: no free pages
[2026-02-12T01:12:10Z] runtime: kv_cache: slot allocation failed: fragmentation>threshold
[2026-02-12T01:12:10Z] runtime: cuda error: out of memory (cuMemAlloc)
[2026-02-12T01:12:11Z] runtime: crash at serve_loop.cc:542 (segfault)
```
That stack + allocator log strongly suggests paged-attn fragmentation and slow leak of resident pages.

oncall-alex: what's the short-term mitigation? we need to reduce customer impact while we fix root cause.

eng-runtime-sam: short-term options (ranked):
1) route a percentage of traffic to smaller model variant (warm fallback) to reduce per-request KV pressure.
2) reduce max_sequence_length at runtime for prod routes for a short window.
3) enable aggressive KV eviction and lower the eviction threshold (hot config) -> immediate memory relief but may increase token latencies or cache misses.
4) cordon+drain worst nodes to stop noisy restarts while we patch.

eng-sre-jess: implementing 3 and 4 in parallel. patching runtime config via redwoodctl and cordoning 3 highest-error nodes.

infra-robin: cordon/drain commands:```
$ kubectl cordon ip-10-0-5-14
$ kubectl drain ip-10-0-5-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```
Draining now, pods relocating to healthier nodes.

eng-runtime-sam: applying hotfix config to lower eviction threshold and enable urgent compaction:```
$ redwoodctl set-config --env prod --key serving.kv.paged.eviction_threshold --value 0.6
$ redwoodctl set-config --env prod --key serving.kv.paged.enable_aggressive_compaction --value true
$ kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving-runtime -n serving
```
This will make allocator reclaim pages earlier. Expect transient 5-15% latency increase and more cache misses.

incident-bot: change recorded: serving.kv.paged.eviction_threshold=0.6 by eng-runtime-sam at 01:22 UTC.

customer-success-lina: I have two customers in the top tier experiencing 502s and increased tail latency. Notified CS reps, opening high-priority RT ticket for affected accounts. ETA update in 30m.

productsupport-matt: got an enterprise escalation on channel from AcmeCorp. they reported model stalls ~01:10 UTC and saw 503s. forwarding notes to customer success.

eng-runtime-sam: after config change, one node showed immediate reduction in resident pages for runtime processes. sample:
before: RSS per process ~28GB -> after: ~20GB
OOM counts dropped from 3/min -> 0 in that instance.

eng-sre-jess: metrics: error rate down from 15% -> 6% in last 4m, CPU stable, token throughput ~70% of baseline. continuing to monitor.

oncall-alex: good. keep the traffic steering to fallback model at 20% for next 30m while we watch. can we capture a heap snapshot / kv map for postmortem? need to avoid further destabilizing nodes.

eng-runtime-sam: agree. taking a single replica snapshot:```
$ redwoodctl debug heap-snapshot --pod svc-infer-abcde-1 --namespace serving --out /tmp/heap-snap-3580011111.gz
```
Will upload to /internal/diagnostics/3580011111 and attach to ticket.

infra-robin: note: one node shows kernel oops interleaved with containerd restarts. I'll open a host ticket and schedule a reboot if it becomes flappy.

eng-sre-jess: also enabling temporary rate limit on the highest-volume routes to blunt load while caches warm:```
$ redwoodctl set-rate-limit --route /v1/generate --limit 1200rps --env prod
```
This is in effect now.

customer-success-lina: informing affected customers: message sent to AcmeCorp and BetaRetail with workaround (retry with smaller batch size, use fallback model). awaiting replies.

eng-runtime-sam: root cause hypothesis: paged-attn allocator fragmentation + slow leakage of resident KV pages on long-tail sequences. Repro steps TBD but likely exacerbated by a workload spike with many long context requests concurrently hitting same node shard. Next steps:
- run offline reproducer against same model with artificial long contexts and KV stress test
- add additional telemetry to track per-shard fragment counts and page occupancy over time
- design a background compaction job to periodically defragment paged allocator without full restart

oncall-alex: handoff plan: I patched eviction threshold and enabled compaction. draining unstable nodes and enabled 20% traffic steer to fallback model. error rate reduced but not back to baseline. I'll stay on for 30m and then hand to next oncall @eng-oncall-2. Please pick up reproducer + telemetry design.

incident-bot: Handoff recorded. oncall-alex -> eng-oncall-2 at 02:00 UTC.

eng-runtime-sam: logging action items: [ACTION] collect heap snapshot (done), [ACTION] run reproducer (assigned sam), [ACTION] telemetry per-shard (assigned runtime team), [ACTION] background compaction RFC (assigned sam).

customer-success-lina: will follow up with customers after we confirm stability and share mitigation timeline.

productsupport-matt: kept AcmeCorp on a call and they saw degraded responses recover after 01:30 UTC. they want a postmortem and SLA credit evaluation.

eng-sre-jess: monitoring 1h window for regression; currently green for OOM spikes. will escalate if reappearance.

oncall-alex: ending active handoff notes: please check /internal/diagnostics/3580011111 for heap snapshot and logs. if OOMs reappear, escalate to oncall-2 + paging.

incident-bot: Thread closed for now; ongoing monitoring."
